ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The account’s biggest missed opportunity is rank-driven on non-brand search: both in-scope non-brand campaigns are losing the majority of eligible impressions to rank (51% lost rank in both), despite only moderate budget loss (14–16%) and plenty of budget headroom (budget utilization ~61–64%). Keyword-level evidence shows multiple high-quality, high-intent terms still sitting at only ~30–36% impression share with 64–70% lost to rank, pointing to bids/ad-rank (and in Hotels & Packages, also quality score) as the main limiter rather than pure budget. A secondary efficiency issue is spend leaking into low-intent service/policy queries (QS 4.0–4.5 with very high CPA), and there’s some waste from competitor-brand “zero-click” impressions that rarely convert.
notable_patterns: Non-brand campaigns are materially constrained by rank: Non-Brand Search - Flights has 33% search impression share with 51% lost to rank (vs 16% lost to budget), and Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages has 35% impression share with 51% lost to rank (vs 14% lost to budget).
Budget is not the binding constraint right now in the two material campaigns: budget utilization is 63.6% (Flights) and 61.4% (Hotels & Packages), indicating headroom while rank loss remains >50%.

Keyword evidence shows strong terms under-delivering due to rank: e.g., “flights to spain” QS 8.5 at 34% IS with 66% lost rank; “all inclusive holidays” QS 8.0 at 36% IS with 64% lost rank; “cheap flights europe” QS 7.5 at 30% IS with 70% lost rank.

Efficiency drag is concentrated in low-quality, high-CPA queries/keywords: “flight booking customer service” QS 4.0 spent £372.28 at £195.94 per conversion, and “hotel cancellation policy” QS 4.5 spent £279.27 at £116.36 per conversion, which is misaligned with non-brand growth goals.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: This campaign is materially missing demand (356,440 missed impressions) and is primarily rank-limited: only 33% impression share with 51% lost to rank vs 16% lost to budget, while budget utilization is only 63.6%. High-QS terms like “cheap flights europe” (QS 7.5) still sit at 30% IS with 70% lost to rank, indicating ad-rank/bid coverage issues rather than demand scarcity.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase coverage on proven high-intent flight terms by raising bids/targets (or loosening bid constraints) specifically where QS is already strong but lost rank is 66–70%; simultaneously add/strengthen intent negatives to cut customer-service leakage (e.g., “customer service”) that carries QS 4.0 and £195.94 CPA.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: This campaign is also materially constrained (300,300 missed impressions) with 35% impression share and 51% lost to rank vs 14% lost to budget, and budget utilization of 61.4%. Unlike Flights, average quality score is weak (5.1), suggesting ad/landing-page relevance is suppressing rank; yet high-QS terms like “all inclusive holidays” (QS 8.0) still only achieve 36% IS with 64% lost rank, implying both bid coverage and quality improvements are needed.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Split/reshape ad groups around top intent themes (all-inclusive, city breaks, packages) to lift QS from the 5.1 baseline and raise bids where QS is already 7–8 but rank loss remains 64–68%; remove negative conflicts (e.g., “visa”) that are blocking relevant demand in this campaign.

recommendation_cards.title: Push high-intent non-brand keywords that already have strong quality scores (rank loss 64–70%)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: In the two material non-brand campaigns, rank is the dominant limiter: both lose 51% of impression share to rank (Flights and Hotels & Packages) while budget utilization is only 63.6% and 61.4%. At the keyword level, several high-QS terms still have very low impression share driven by rank loss: “cheap flights europe” (QS 7.5) at 30% IS with 70% lost rank; “flights to spain” (QS 8.5) at 34% IS with 66% lost rank; “all inclusive holidays” (QS 8.0) at 36% IS with 64% lost rank; “weekend city breaks” (QS 7.0) at 32% IS with 68% lost rank.
recommended_steps: Increase bids/targets specifically on the listed high-QS, high-rank-loss keywords (or move them into a dedicated high-priority ad group/campaign with more aggressive targets).
Apply device/geo/daypart bid adjustments only if they protect ROI; otherwise prioritize regaining lost rank on these terms first.
Re-check impression share lost to rank weekly on these exact keywords and keep lifting until rank loss is no longer the majority driver.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: For the four named keywords, impression share moving from ~30–36% toward 45%+ while lost-to-rank drops from ~64–70% toward <45%.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix Hotels & Packages quality score drag (avg QS 5.1) to regain rank without overpaying
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages has a low average quality score (5.1) alongside 51% impression share lost to rank and only 61.4% budget utilization. Keyword evidence suggests QS is tightly linked to impression share (pearson r = 0.957), so lifting QS in this campaign should translate into materially better coverage at similar CPCs.
recommended_steps: Restructure into tighter intent groupings (e.g., separate “all inclusive holidays”, “city breaks”, “hotel + flight packages”) and ensure each group has aligned headlines/descriptions and a matching landing page.
Write/refresh one additional ad per core ad group to reach/maintain top ad strength while explicitly mirroring the user’s intent (destination + package type) in primary headlines.
Audit landing pages for message match (packages vs hotels-only vs city breaks) and improve above-the-fold relevance to those themes before raising bids broadly.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Campaign-level avg quality score in Hotels & Packages improving from 5.1 toward 6.0+ and impression share lost to rank falling below 45%.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop paying for low-intent service/policy queries that carry very high CPA and low QS
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The worst efficiency is concentrated in non-booking intent: “flight booking customer service” has QS 4.0 with £372.28 spend and £195.94 cost per conversion; “hotel cancellation policy” has QS 4.5 with £279.27 spend and £116.36 cost per conversion. These terms also depress overall ad-rank dynamics because low QS increases the cost to win auctions.
recommended_steps: Add/expand intent negatives in non-brand campaigns for customer-service and policy research themes (e.g., customer service, phone number, contact, cancellation policy, refund policy, complaints), while allowing exceptions where you truly want that traffic.
Separate any unavoidable support/service demand into its own low-bid campaign (or ad group) with capped bids so it cannot compete with booking-intent terms.
Review the search terms weekly and block new variants that match the same service/policy intent pattern.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Spend share on service/policy themes trending down and blended cost per conversion improving (target: remove the £195.94 and £116.36 CPA outliers from the top-spend term set).

recommendation_cards.title: Remove negative-keyword conflicts that are blocking relevant non-brand demand (1,790 blocked impressions)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The negative-keyword conflicts report shows 2 conflicts blocking an estimated 1,790 impressions: negative “jobs” blocks “flight attendant jobs cheap flights europe” in Non-Brand Search - Flights (640 blocked impressions) and negative “visa” blocks “weekend city breaks visa requirements” in Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages (1,150 blocked impressions). With both campaigns already rank-limited (51% lost rank), these conflicts further reduce reach in already under-delivering areas.
recommended_steps: Convert the conflicting negatives into more precise variants (e.g., apply as exact/phrase where appropriate) or scope them to the specific ad groups where they’re truly needed.
If those queries are genuinely irrelevant, add a cleaner negative that blocks the intent without colliding with valuable themes (e.g., block “flight attendant jobs” rather than broad “jobs”).
After changes, re-check the conflicts report to confirm blocked impressions drop toward zero while irrelevant traffic doesn’t return.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Estimated blocked impressions falling from 1,790 toward ~0, with no rebound in low-intent conversion rates.

already_working: Brand Search - UK is highly profitable and not a top opportunity cost: ROAS is 48.18 with strong scale (790.3 conversions, £464,047.33 revenue) and budget utilization is only 58.5%, so it’s not the main constraint relative to non-brand missed impressions.

Ad creation/execution is generally solid: 83.3% of ads are rated Excellent or Good (4 Excellent, 1 Good out of 6), so the account’s biggest gains are more likely from rank/bid coverage and keyword/query controls than from a full ad rewrite.

Competitive positioning isn’t broadly weak at the account level: avg top-of-page rate is higher for you (66.3%) than the named competitor benchmark (53.9%), and your avg outranking share is 61.4%, suggesting the most acute rank issues are concentrated in specific non-brand auctions/keywords rather than a universal inability to compete.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: Non-brand is currently rank-constrained while the travel search market is accelerating: external data shows both (a) strong growth in exactly the high-intent flight queries you’re under-serving due to lost rank, and (b) rising search spend in your core (UK) market—meaning auctions are likely getting more competitive. Acting now to lift Ad Rank (bids + QS) should help you capture this expanding demand before incremental competitor spend further pushes you down the page, while cleaning up low-intent leakage protects efficiency as CPC pressure rises.

supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Because the account diagnosis shows “flights to spain” already has strong QS (8.5) but low impression share driven by rank loss, this +51% demand growth increases the opportunity cost of staying rank-limited right now.

supporting_facts.fact: Deal-seeking flight intent is rising: “budget airline flight deals” grows from 100 (Q4 2025) to 141 (Q3 2026), i.e., +41%.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Supports urgency to increase rank coverage on non-brand flight terms (via bids/targets) while you still have budget headroom—growth in ‘deals’ intent implies more competition and more available volume to win if rank improves.

supporting_facts.fact: Another non-brand flight-intent segment is accelerating: “last minute flights europe” grows from 100 (Q4 2025) to 156 (Q3 2026), i.e., +56%.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Reinforces that non-brand flight auctions are expanding quickly; if you remain rank-limited (as the account shows), you’ll miss a growing share of incremental demand.

supporting_facts.fact: In the United Kingdom (pilot account market), Search Spend Growth QoQ is 22.0%.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Rising spend is a proxy for intensifying auction pressure; with the account already losing the majority of eligible impressions to rank (not budget), waiting likely makes it harder/more expensive to regain lost impression share later.

supporting_facts.fact: A key competitor (Horizon Holidays) holds 16% spend share vs the Pilot Account at 14.0% spend share.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Suggests competitive presence is slightly ahead of you; in a rank-constrained situation, even modest competitor spend advantages can translate into outsized lost impression share—supporting immediate action to defend/improve Ad Rank.

supporting_facts.fact: Search represents 41% share of category spend (Share of Category Spend = 41%).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Validates that search is a primary battleground in this vertical; because your biggest issue is search rank loss on non-brand, improvements here directly address the highest-leverage channel as spend concentrates there.

email_copy.subject: GBP 316,559 sitting in rank loss (37.84% IS; 47.0% lost to rank)
email_copy.hook: Looking at your paid search account, the constraint isn’t budget — it’s where you’re showing up (or not) on non-brand. You’ve got meaningful headroom off a GBP 6,200 daily budget, but you’re still giving up the bulk of eligible impressions because Ad Rank isn’t clearing the auctions consistently.
why_now_bullets: UK search auctions are heating up: Search Spend Growth QoQ is 22.0%, which typically pushes CPCs and makes lost rank harder to win back later.
The exact flight demand you’re currently under-serving is accelerating: “flights to spain” is up +51% (index 100 -> 151), so staying rank-limited now has a higher opportunity cost.
Competitors are leaning in: one key competitor holds 16% spend share vs your 14.0% — in a rank-constrained account, that small gap can translate into a big share of missed non-brand clicks.
email_copy.stat_sub: What you can unlock by fixing rank limits + cutting low-intent leakage
email_copy.impact_line: The account is currently capped by visibility: with impression share at 37.84% and 47.0% lost to rank (vs 15.2% lost to budget), you’re not losing because you ran out of spend — you’re losing because you’re getting pushed down the page on high-intent non-brand queries. That’s why the near-term upside penciled out at GBP 316,559 for this quarter.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is the campaign-level view of where that upside is concentrated, so you can see exactly where rank pressure is costing you the most.
email_copy.cards_intro: Net: your best-performing non-brand demand is being throttled by Ad Rank, while a smaller slice of spend is drifting into queries that don’t signal booking intent. The fixes below are prioritized to win more of the right auctions first, then tighten efficiency so you don’t pay more than you have to.
email_copy.working_intro: Also worth noting: there are a few things you’re already doing well — so this is more about reallocating weight and removing friction than rebuilding the account.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If we lift coverage modestly and clean up the drag, the math turns into real volume fast — the opportunity sizing below shows the incremental impressions and clicks that bridge directly to that GBP 316,559 upside.
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map this into a 14-day action plan in your account?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with “Tue” or “Thu” and I’ll send two specific time options for a 20-minute working session. If you’d rather keep it async, just reply “plan” and I’ll send the exact build order + what to watch each week.
email_copy.ps: P.S. Because your constraint is rank (not spend), the quickest wins usually come from targeted bid/QS lifts on proven intent — not from increasing budgets across the board.
